chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi and Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu al-Subbah, all of them, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): In

two men who shared in property, and they made a profit from it, and among that property was a debt and a physical asset. One of them said to his partner: 'Give me the principal capital, and the profit is yours, and whatever I owe (or you owe) is upon you.' He said (peace be upon him): 'There is no harm in it if it is stipulated, and even if the stipulation contradicts the Book of Allah, it is referred back to the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on a partnership where one partner takes the principal and the other takes the profit?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates a specific partnership arrangement where one partner assumes the principal capital while the other takes the profit, provided the condition is explicitly stipulated. The Imam clarifies that even if the stipulation seems to contradict general legal principles, it remains valid as long as it is ultimately referred back to the Book of Allah, highlighting the Shia juristic emphasis on contractual flexibility and the supremacy of divine text over rigid analogical reasoning.
